decision: Restore both implementations. A has no demonstrated useful complete-operation gain; B does not remove the observed spilled span state and is stopped before an uninstrumented screen. No family ban or source-count CPU claim.

hypotheses.A: Advance existing safe vector-span views by four vectors rather than keep a growing vector index and compute four index-to-byte addresses per group. Keep fixed0/1/2/3 loads-before-stores, remaining-vector and byte tails. No gain follows from source/code size or partial software samples; memory traffic or new span guards can offset the change.
hypotheses.B: Keep the advancing-vector kernel behind one noninlined shared call so its span state is not merged into large caller EH loops. Current A generated fixed offsets but spilled mutable span fields each group: flip894->1093B,Clone640->963B; screens inconclusive/adverse. This is a changed architecture/producer, not a favorable A timing retry.

endState.A: One shared disjoint-copy primitive with advancing local views; all existing callers, portable/small fallback, output allocation, admission, ownership and cooperative checkpoints unchanged. No new kernel family, cache, buffer, session, owner, unchecked API or fixture dispatch.
endState.B: One shared safe independent-copy implementation and unchanged small/portable path; fewer duplicated inlined bodies. No owner/cache/buffer/session/API, fixture-specific dispatch or unchecked memory access. Per-call overhead may outweigh any simplification, especially per-row flips; no benefit assumed.
